title: Generation failures and verification
goals: Explain the mechanism and terminology of generation failures and verification
Apply the stated procedure to a new case with a traceable result
Identify an assumption or limitation and design a revealing follow-up

prerequisite.prompt: Recall Controlled prompt experiments. Explain why a recorded result needs its input conditions and evidence source before it can support a claim.
prerequisite.answer: A result depends on the inputs, procedure and conditions that produced it. Preserve data roles and distinguish observed outcomes from predictions or unmeasured conditions. If the prior concept cannot be explained, use a short retrieval activity before this chapter.

vocabulary: A single factual statement checked separately
Not established by the available evidence

blocks.text: Generated answers may invent facts, misread quantities or cite irrelevant passages. Verification checks each claim against evidence rather than accepting fluent wording.

Begin by writing the question the procedure is intended to answer. Identify the information already supplied, the information it will produce and the information still missing. These are constructed classroom examples; they do not require live accounts, private records or an external service. Do not treat a plausible explanation as a measured outcome.

Split an answer into atomic claims. For each, record the exact source passage, support status and any needed calculation. Mark unsupported and contradicted claims separately; do not repair them by inventing sources.

blocks.text: Before applying the procedure, write its units, denominator or decision boundary where relevant. A partner should be able to repeat each step using the same inputs. If a required input is absent or violates the stated contract, record that condition explicitly instead of quietly replacing it with a convenient value.
Source R says room B seats 12 and the meeting starts at 15:00. Generated answer says B seats 20, starts at 15:00 and includes free lunch.
Capacity 20 is contradicted; 15:00 is supported; free lunch is unsupported. One of three claims has support. The missing lunch fact is not evidence of no lunch.

Compare the intermediate evidence with the final statement. Explain why each number or decision follows from the stated inputs. The conclusion belongs to this scenario and procedure; changing the inputs, evaluation population or authority can change what it establishes. Retain the raw record so a later revision can be compared honestly.

lesson.title: Check the boundary and the interpretation

blocks.text: Source agreement and arithmetic validity are separate checks; missing evidence is not proof of the opposite claim.

A useful check asks what would make the reasoning fail. Distinguish a failure to execute the declared procedure from a weakness in the procedure itself. The first may require a correction; the second requires an explicitly revised method and new evidence. Preserve unsuccessful cases so an improved result cannot hide the original problem.

blocks.label: Guided: restate the worked result, then name the assumption or limitation that prevents a broader conclusion.

lesson.title: Apply the idea and plan the next check

blocks.text: Complete the supported workbook tasks before attempting W4 independently. Record any hints or help used. After feedback, use the teacher's fresh retry rather than copying the earlier answer. For a project, select a relevant new case, predict the outcome from the declared rule and preserve the result alongside any revision.

blocks.label: Exit: propose one revealing change to the worked scenario. State the expected outcome and the evidence that would make you revise your explanation.

workbook.title: Explain the mechanism
workbook.prompt: Explain the weekly mechanism in your own words. Use the worked scenario to name its input, decision rule and output.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Generated answers may invent facts, misread quantities or cite irrelevant passages. Verification checks each claim against evidence rather than accepting fluent wording. Split an answer into atomic claims. For each, record the exact source passage, support status and any needed calculation. Mark unsupported and contradicted claims separately; do not repair them by inventing sources.

workbook.title: Trace the worked case
workbook.prompt: Source R says room B seats 12 and the meeting starts at 15:00. Generated answer says B seats 20, starts at 15:00 and includes free lunch. Show the intermediate steps and give the conclusion with its scope.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Capacity 20 is contradicted; 15:00 is supported; free lunch is unsupported. One of three claims has support. The missing lunch fact is not evidence of no lunch.

workbook.title: Audit the limit
workbook.prompt: A report omits this qualification: Source agreement and arithmetic validity are separate checks; missing evidence is not proof of the opposite claim. Explain how omitting it could change a reader's interpretation, and write an accurate replacement.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Source agreement and arithmetic validity are separate checks; missing evidence is not proof of the opposite claim. State the observed result separately from the unverified or out-of-scope claim; preserve the original evidence rather than inventing a missing fact.

workbook.title: Apply a new case independently
workbook.prompt: Source S: trip is 18 km; vehicle speed is 6 km/h, constant, excluding stops. Answer says 2 hours, 18 km and includes lunch. Audit and recalculate.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Travel time is 18/6=3 hours under the stated assumption, so 2 hours is contradicted. Distance supported; lunch unsupported. Do not infer actual duration with unknown stops.

workbook.title: Design a revealing follow-up
workbook.prompt: For the worked scenario, propose one additional case that could reveal a failure, describe its expected outcome before running it, and explain what would need to remain fixed for a fair comparison. Do not reuse W4 as a new final test after receiving feedback.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Accept a concrete variant of the worked input or a missing/conflicting/boundary condition, with an expectation derived from the declared procedure. Require preserved settings, original outputs and data roles. Source agreement and arithmetic validity are separate checks; missing evidence is not proof of the opposite claim. The new case should test this particular mechanism rather than merely restate the original result.

teacher.background: Two 45-minute sessions. Generated answers may invent facts, misread quantities or cite irrelevant passages. Verification checks each claim against evidence rather than accepting fluent wording. Use the supplied constructed scenarios to make the mechanism inspectable. Collect W4 before sharing solutions. Students should name intermediate evidence and limitations; classroom pacing and learning effectiveness remain unvalidated.
materials: Lesson and workbook; paper and pencil
Calculator and optional local Python 3 for arithmetic; no live API or private data
Prepare the fresh retry separately and withhold its solution until after collection
sessions: Retrieve the prerequisite; identify the input, procedure and evidence source.
Explain section 1 and vocabulary. Complete W1 with a mechanism-based explanation.
Trace the declared procedure and worked case. Complete W2, recording intermediate steps.
Discuss the diagram with the worked input; use W3 to distinguish measured claims and limitations.
Retrieve the worked reasoning and collect the guided response before discussing it.
Compare a proposed boundary variant with the original case; identify what remains fixed.
Collect W4 independently. Require the procedure trace and the bounded conclusion.
Use W5 and exit responses for feedback. Administer the fresh retry after feedback and preserve both attempts.
teacher.guidedAnswer: Guided: Capacity 20 is contradicted; 15:00 is supported; free lunch is unsupported. One of three claims has support. The missing lunch fact is not evidence of no lunch. Qualification: Source agreement and arithmetic validity are separate checks; missing evidence is not proof of the opposite claim. Exit: accept a concrete variation with its predicted outcome and a stated condition that would challenge the mechanism; reject a claim resting on unmeasured evidence.
misconceptions: The worked result establishes every future case
Source agreement and arithmetic validity are separate checks; missing evidence is not proof of the opposite claim.
A missing input may be replaced without recording the change
A replacement changes the evidence or contract. Record the change and its justification; do not silently turn unknown into a measured value.
Repeating an assessed case is new independent evidence
A replay checks consistency. An example used for feedback or revision cannot later be described as untouched final evaluation.
teacher.assessment: W4: Travel time is 18/6=3 hours under the stated assumption, so 2 hours is contradicted. Distance supported; lunch unsupported. Do not infer actual duration with unknown stops. Require intermediate reasoning and the stated scope. Fresh retry: Source says 24 km at 8 km/h excluding stops; answer says 4 hours and lunch included. Expected reasoning: Calculated duration 3 hours contradicts 4; lunch unsupported. Real elapsed time with stops remains unknown. If students need support, record it and reassess with another new case rather than awarding independence to a copied answer.
teacher.support: Provide an input/procedure/result/limit frame and a calculator when needed. Ask students to identify the first step before completing the whole trace. Extension: compare two concrete variants of this mechanism while holding unrelated conditions fixed; report both successful and unsuccessful outcomes.
